O.outcome_detail: representation and emphasis in the literature

cells.quote:
Formal training is the most consistently described source of knowledge for managing OEs.

Accounts of workplace-based learning (WPBL) from real-patient encounters—whether as part of formal training or arising organically from clinical work—are sparse.
cells.note: The review reports greater representation of formal training than WPBL, rather than a comparative learning outcome.

D.comparison: making learning visible and informing workplace practice

cells.quote: Few studies describe strategies to make this learning visible (OE308),24 with assessment of knowledge being the primary focus (OE34,25 OE178,26 OE97,27 OE227,28 OE59,29 OE7,30 OE286,31 OE325).32 Similarly, while course evaluations are common—using tests (OE171,33 OE195,34 OE103,35 OE159)36 and novel self-assessment tools (OE226)37 or video observation (OE149)38—how such assessments themselves act as a source of knowledge, or inform future workplace practice, is under-investigated.
cells.note: The study contrasts assessment-focused reporting with the under-investigated use of assessment to inform workplace practice; no direct learner-performance effect is reported.
